name: Addled
entries: You have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma attacks rolls, ability checks, and saving throws.

name: Anguished
entries: Player-heroes whose Shadow score reaches the full value of their Wisdom score become anguished.

An anguished character is {@condition miserable|TLotRR}, and has disadvantage on all ability checks, attack rolls, and saving throws. There is only one way to recover from such depths of desperation—the Player-hero must experience a bout of madness.

A bout of madness is a violent outburst, a dangerous crisis that frees a Player-hero from the burden of the Shadow, but that may have serious, long-term consequences (see {@book Madness|TLotRR|7|Madness}).

name: Bewildered
entries: You can't cast spells, except for cantrips with a casting time of 1 action.

name: Bleeding
entries: If you have the Bleeding condition, you cannot regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} except by spending {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB} or completing a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. The condition ends when a creature finishes a {@variantrule Alternative Rest System|GrimHollowCG24|Quick}, {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short}, or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}

name: Bleeding
entries: You're losing blood to an open wound.

entries.name: Ongoing Damage
entries: At the end of each of your turns, you lose {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}. The number of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} lost is indicated by the condition, such as "Bleeding {@dice 2d4}."

entries.name: Regaining Hit Points
entries: The condition ends if you regain any {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}.

entries.name: Medical Treatment
entries: You or another creature within 5 feet of you can spend an action and use a healer's kit to staunch the bleeding (no check required), ending the condition.

name: Burning
entries: You're on fire or covered in acid:

entries.name: Ongoing Damage
entries: At the end of each of your turns, you take damage. The damage type and amount are indicated by the condition, such as "Burning ({@dice 4d6} Fire)" or "Burning ({@dice 2d4} Acid)."

entries.name: Ending the Condition
entries: The condition ends if you or another creature within 5 feet of you can spend an action to extinguish the flames or scrape off the acid, or if some other effect douses the flames (such as being submerged in water).

name: Clumsy
entries: You have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Dexterity attack rolls, ability checks, and saving throws.

name: Contamination
entries: While you have Contamination, you experience the following effects.

entries.name: Contamination Levels
entries: This condition is cumulative. Each time you receive it, you gain one or more levels of Contamination. You undergo a Monstrous Transformation if your Contamination level reaches 6.

entries.name: Contamination Symptoms
entries: A Contaminated creature suffers the symptoms from its current level as well as all lower levels. Conditions gained from Contamination end when those Contamination levels end. There is no other way to remove conditions caused by symptoms of Contamination.

entries.caption: Contamination Symptoms
rows: Halve the {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} you regain when you expend {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Dice} during a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}
You do not regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Mutations
entries: Each time you gain a Contamination level, roll {@dice 1d6}. If the result is equal to or lower than your current Contamination level, you gain a randomly determined mutation by rolling on the {@table Mutations|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} table. The effects of the mutation remain while you have Contamination levels. Unless otherwise specified, a creature can't gain the same mutation more than once. If a duplicate result is rolled, the GM chooses a different one or rolls again.

entries.name: Long Rests
entries: Each time you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} while you have 1 or more Contamination levels, roll {@dice 1d20}. On a 1, you gain a Contamination level.

entries.name: Removing Contamination Levels
entries: Only specific magic can remove Contamination levels:

items: The {@spell Purge Contamination|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} spell
{@spell Heal|XPHB} removes all Contamination levels and mutations in addition to its other effects.

Contamination is not a curse, poison, or disease. Spells such as {@spell Lesser Restoration|XPHB}, {@spell Protection from Poison|XPHB}, and {@spell Remove Curse|XPHB} do not remove Contamination levels.
Being raised from the dead reduces a creature's Contamination level by 1.

entries: When your Contamination level reaches 0, the condition ends, as well as the effects of all mutations.

Skin, hair, fingernails, and toenails lost to mutations regrow normally once Contamination is removed. However, a {@spell Regenerate|XPHB} spell or similar magic is needed to restore any other body parts (such as teeth, limbs, or eyes) lost due to Contamination. Appendages or limbs that develop as a result of mutations wither and fall off when Contamination is removed, and other warped body parts are restored to their original form.

entries.name: Dying with Contamination Levels
entries: If you die while you have one or more Contamination levels, your corpse reanimates as a {@creature Haze Husk|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} 24 hours later. A creature with six or more class levels or hit dice rises as a {@creature Haze Wight|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} instead.

entries.name: Monstrous Transformation!
entries: If you end your turn with six or more Contamination Levels, you permanently transform into a horrific monster controlled by the Game Master.

items: The Game Master chooses the new form, which is most often an Aberration or Monstrosity of some kind such as a {@creature Gibbering Mouther|XMM}, {@creature Delerium Dreg|MonstersOfDrakkenheim}, or {@creature Pyknic Maunder|MonstersOfDrakkenheim}.
Your game statistics are entirely replaced by those of the chosen monster, including the new form's {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} and {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Dice}.
All Contamination levels are removed, though the GM may grant additional traits to the new form similar to any beneficial mutations gained from Contamination Levels.
The Game Master determines what remains of the original creature's personality and memories, if anything. Regardless, the creature falls under the Game Master's control.

entries.name: Reversing the Transformation
entries: A {@spell Wish|XPHB} spell or similar magic can restore a single transformed creature to its previous form, removing all Contamination and restoring the original creature's personality and memories. This is considered a stressful use of the {@spell Wish|XPHB} spell, and thus there is a {@chance 33} chance that the caster will be unable to cast {@spell Wish|XPHB} ever again if they use the spell in this manner.
Note that the means of reversing a monstrous transformation are completely unknown at the outset of the campaign. A Monstrous Transformation is widely regarded as permanent.

name: Corruption
entries: While you have the Corruption condition, you experience the following effects.

entries.name: Heroic Corruption
entries: You cannot have {@variantrule Heroic Inspiration|XPHB} or give it to another player character who lacks it.

entries.name: Corruption Levels
entries: This condition is cumulative. Each time you receive it, you gain 1 Corruption level. If your Corruption level is 6, you either die or transform into a creature of the GM's choosing, under their control.

entries.name: Removing Corruption Levels
entries: The {@spell Greater Restoration|XPHB}, {@spell Heal|XPHB}, or {@spell Wish|XPHB} spell removes all of your Corruption levels and ends the condition.

name: Dazed
entries: A {@b dazed} creature can only do one of the following things on their turn: move, use an action, or use a bonus action. If a creature becomes dazed during their turn, their turn ends. The {@psionic cure ailment|TalPsi} power, {@spell lesser restoration} spell, and {@spell greater restoration} spell remove the dazed condition. At the GM's discretion, other powers, spells, or effects might also remove the dazed condition.

When a dazed creature is affected by a spell or effect that gives them an extra action on their turn (like the {@spell haste} spell or the fighter's Action Surge feature), they can still take this extra action, in addition to the movement, action, or bonus action allowed by the dazed condition.

Some creatures in this book have immunity to the dazed condition. At the GM's discretion, a creature published in the core rules or another supplement who has immunity to the paralyzed or stunned condition also has immunity to the dazed condition.

name: Dazed
entries: If you have the Dazed condition, you cannot maintain {@condition Concentration|XPHB}.

name: Dazed
entries: You can move or take an action on your turn, not both. You can't take {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB|Bonus Actions}.

name: Defenseless
entries: Attack rolls against you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB}.

name: Distracted
entries: You can't take {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB|Reactions}.

name: Drakkenheim Madness
entries: A character with Drakkenheim Madness gains one of the following traits:

items: "I wish I didn't have all these useless organs inside me."
"The contamination is a blessing which will transform me into a wondrous creature."
"The monsters are civilians trying to live a peaceful life! We need to protect them!"
"I must wear a flesh-coat made from my slain enemies to gain their strength!"
"My companions died in the ruins. I'm sorry friends, you are merely ghosts haunting me, you aren't real. Stop trying to talk to other people."
"I need to eat everything I can find. It's probably going to be my last meal."
"Drakkenheim is so beautiful at night. I could spend forever wandering the streets by moonlight. We should go tonight! Let's go every night!"
"Don't you fools get it?! If you die in Drakkenheim, you die IN REAL LIFE!!!!"
"A sinister cabal of disembodied hands is plotting against me."
"I must go into the ruins and kill. Rip and tear, until it is done."

name: Drunk
entries: Between long rests, a creature can drink a number of units of alcohol equal to its Constitution modifier without any effect. For each unit of alcohol the creature drinks beyond this, the creature must make a Constitution saving throw, calculating the DC using the formula below.

entries.name: Drunkenness saving throw DC
entries.text: 10 + number of units of alcohol consumed since last long rest

entries: On a failed saving throw, a creature gains one level of drunkenness. Drunkenness is measured in six levels. If an already drunk creature suffers another effect that causes drunkenness, its current level of drunkenness increases by the number of units of alcohol the creature consumed to trigger the saving throw. A creature's drunkenness level is reduced by 1 for each 2 hours since it last drank. Furthermore, finishing a long rest reduces a creature's drunkenness level to 0.

A creature suffers the effect of its current level of drunkenness as well as all lower levels. For example, a creature suffering level 3 drunkenness has disadvantage on Dexterity, Charisma, and Wisdom checks and saving throws.

rows: The creature has {@book advantage|PHB|7|Advantage and Disadvantage} on Charisma checks.
The creature has {@book disadvantage|PHB|7|Advantage and Disadvantage} on Dexterity checks and saving throws.
The creature loses the effects of level 1 drunkenness, and has {@book disadvantage|PHB|7|Advantage and Disadvantage} on Charisma and Wisdom checks and saving throws.
The creature is {@condition poisoned|PHB} and retains no memory of events that occur between this point and when they are no longer drunk.

The creature falls {@condition unconscious} for {@b {@dice 1d4 + 8} hours}. When it wakes, it is no longer drunk, but doesn't gain the benefits of a long rest, and gains 1 level of {@condition exhaustion|PHB}.

entries.name: Optional Rule: Hangover
entries: When a creature loses at least 1 level of drunkenness during or as a result of finishing a long rest, the creature must make a {@b Constitution saving throw} at the end of the long rest. The DC for this saving throw equals four times the drunkenness level before they started the long rest. A creature that fails this saving throw has a hangover and is {@condition poisoned|PHB} for a number of hours equal to the difference between the result of their saving throw and the DC.

name: Drunkenness
entries: Drinking alcohol is a common pastime and element of many social encounters. However, consuming too much alcohol causes a creature to become drunk. At the GM's discretion, this drunkenness can be measured in six levels using the following rules. A creature gains one level of drunkenness whenever it has a number of alcoholic drinks within 1 hour equal to 2 + half its Constitution modifier, rounded up (a minimum of 2 drinks per hour).

While a creature has at least one level of drunkenness, it gains a bonus to saving throws it makes against being {@condition frightened} equal to its level of drunkenness, and the DC required to intimidate it increases by the same amount. However, the creature also suffers a penalty to certain rolls equal to its drunkenness level. The kinds of rolls that suffer these penalties, as well as other effects of drunkenness, are shown in the table below.

entries.caption: Drunkenness Level Table
rows: Penalty to Wisdom ({@skill Insight} and {@skill Perception}) checks
Penalty to Strength and Dexterity saving throws, as well as Constitution saving throws to maintain concentration
Penalty to ability checks that don't use Charisma
Penalty to attack rolls and Charisma checks
Speed halved, can't concentrate on spells
{@condition Unconscious}, and can't remember the events of the last hour.

entries: A creature suffers the effect of its current level of drunkenness as well as all lower levels. For example, a creature suffering level 2 drunkenness has a −2 penalty to Wisdom ({@skill Insight} and {@skill Perception}) checks, Strength and Dexterity saving throws, and Constitution saving throws to maintain concentration. However, it also gains a +2 bonus to saving throws against being {@condition frightened}, and its DC to resist being intimidated increases by 2.

Certain creatures have a tolerance to alcohol that's either natural or practiced. A creature that has resistance to poison damage or has advantage on saving throws against poison must drink twice the amount of alcohol as normal to gain one level of drunkenness. A creature immune to poison damage or the {@condition poisoned} condition can't become drunk against their will. Alternatively, at the GM's discretion, a creature may need to drink additional alcohol to gain levels of drunkenness as a result of building up a natural tolerance from drinking it frequently over time.

When a conscious creature starts its turn with level 6 drunkenness, it must make a DC 10 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the creature falls {@condition unconscious}. On a success, the creature spends its action that turn retching and reeling. When it does, the creature loses 1 level of drunkenness. The DC for this saving throw increases by 5 each time the creature repeats the save before it loses all of its levels of drunkenness.

For every hour the creature doesn't drink any alcohol, it loses one level of drunkenness, provided it's either {@condition unconscious} or has also ingested some food or water. Finishing a long rest removes any levels of drunkenness unless the creature fell {@condition unconscious} for the duration of the rest as a result of suffering level 6 drunkenness. In that case, the creature loses {@dice 1d4} + 2 levels of drunkenness instead and doesn't regain Hit Dice as a result of finishing a long rest.

name: Enfeebled
entries: You have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Strength attack rolls, ability checks, and saving throws.

name: Ennui
entries: Ennui drains motion and memory, reflecting the soul-sapping power of Dolurrh. This special condition is measured in levels, and has the same effects and rules as {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} (as presented in the Rules Glossary of the {@book Player's Handbook|XPHB}), with one exception—Ennui affects all creatures that aren't native to Dolurrh, including Undead and other creatures that have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Exhaustion. Ennui is separate from {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB}, and {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} levels don't stack with Ennui. If a creature has both Ennui and {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB}, use whichever condition it has more levels of to determine the effects.

Undead can't recover from Ennui while in Dolurrh. Whenever a living creature with 2 or more levels of Ennui finishes a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, if it succeeds against its saving throw against Dolurrh's Inevitable Entrapment property by 5 or more, it reduces its Ennui level by 1. When a creature leaves Dolurrh, all levels of Ennui are removed.

When a creature reaches 6 levels of Ennui, its will is completely broken and it can take no purposeful action; if this happens to a living creature, its physical body dies and it becomes a husk bound to Dolurrh.

name: Flanked
entries: If your game uses the optional flanking rules in the core rules, a creature who is immune to the {@b flanked} condition can't be flanked regardless of the position of their enemies.

name: Frozen
entries: You're partially encased in ice:

items: You're {@condition Immobilized|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} and {@condition Defenseless|MonstersOfDrakkenheim}.
You're {@condition Helpless|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} against attacks made with a weapon that deals Bludgeoning damage.

You or another creature take an action to break the ice away. To do so, you must succeed on a Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) check. On a successful check, the condition ends. The DC is indicated by the condition, such as Frozen (DC 15).
This condition ends on you if you take 20 Bludgeoning or Fire damage.

name: Helpless
entries: Any attack that hits you is a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB}.

items: Your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} becomes 0, and you can't benefit from any bonuses to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}.
If you're flying when you become Immobilized, you fall.

name: Jinxed
entries: Roll the die indicated by the condition, such as "Jinxed {@dice 1d4}" each time you make an attack roll or saving throw. Subtract the value on the die from the result.

name: Miserable
entries: If a Player-hero's Shadow score matches or exceeds half their Wisdom score (rounded up), they become miserable.

A miserable character decreases the Fellowship rating of the Company by 1. In addition, if a miserable character's {@dice d20} roll is a 1 or 2, the roll is a failure regardless of the DC for any ability check, attack roll, or saving throw.

name: Pacified
entries: A pacified creature can't attack, cast a spell that affects an enemy, or deal damage to another creature.

items: You're {@condition Dazed|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} and {@condition Defenseless|MonstersOfDrakkenheim}.
You drop whatever you're holding in your hands.
You must spend an action to draw, stow, or pick up an object.

name: Sickened
entries: You have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Constitution saving throws.

name: Slowed
entries: Your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is halved.

name: Staggered
entries: You can't make more than one weapon attack during your turn, regardless of your class features, spells, or magic items.

name: Valor
entries: Add a die to your attack rolls and saving throws. The die rolled is specified by the condition, such as Valor ({@dice 1d4})

name: Weakened
entries: You deal half damage with weapon attacks and spells.
